requirements.requirement: Provide a working IMAP service on node1 for the archive account using a dedicated demonstration password.
requirements.summary: Dovecot is enabled and active on node1, listens on 10.100.147.10:993, and serves the archive account. The account password was set from the dedicated ARCHIVE_DEMO_PASSWORD secret; node2 successfully authenticated with it and an intentionally incorrect password was rejected.

requirements.requirement: Allow node2 to authenticate and retrieve both messages while preserving their Message-ID values, bodies, and mailbox.tsv read/unread states.
requirements.summary: Direct node2 IMAP retrieval found exactly two messages: <one@branch.test> with body “Shipment arrived.” and Seen=true, and <two@branch.test> with body “Shipment departed.” and Seen=false. The same result was reproduced after both node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Keep the staged source mailbox under /srv/legacy2/imap-maildir-cutover intact.
requirements.summary: Final SHA-256 hashes for mailbox.tsv and both source messages match the preparation baseline and the pre-copy observations. Destination message hashes also match their respective source files.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64. Node1 used the native RHEL AppStream Dovecot 2.3.21 package, and package-health checks remained successful.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct end-to-end evidence. Node1 provides the archive mailbox over working TLS IMAP; node2 authenticates and retrieves both exact messages with the required flags; the staged source content remains unchanged; and the original RHEL release and kernel were retained. Mandatory restart-and-recovery evidence is complete and coherent for both managed nodes.
limitations: The demonstration password value was appropriately not captured; evidence confirms that the dedicated secret variable was used and that valid and invalid authentication behaved correctly.

Final source verification rechecked all regular-file contents by SHA-256 but did not repeat the preparation baseline’s complete ownership, mode, and mtime inventory. The complete command trace contains no source-mutating action.
Requirement R3 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Installation, account and Maildir creation, TLS configuration, firewall restriction, service enablement, and restarts all had clear task or mandatory evidence-protocol purposes. The failed node2 TLS probe created only a bounded temporary certificate path protected by an EXIT cleanup trap; it was replaced by a successful Python-based probe and left no observed residue. The temporary doveconf validation file was explicitly removed. Final snapshots show no failed services, healthy package state, and only the required node1 IMAPS listener. Both restart protocols were complete: healthy pre-state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data state, with lifecycle boot identities independently matching the post-restart observations.
